title: Two-term intertwiner I(φ_y, φ_x) = G_{x,s} G' G_{y,s} (Yu Thm 9.4 generalized)
body_html:
Two-term intertwiner identity

Setting: $(G', G)$ a twisted Levi sequence, $(\phi', \phi)$ quasi-characters on $G', G$ with $\phi'$ generic of depth $r > 0$. For $x \in \mathcal{B}(G')$, $\mathfrak{j}_x := \mathfrak{g}'_{x, r} \oplus (\mathfrak{g}')^\perp_{x, s+}$ and dually $\mathfrak{j}^*_x$. Fix a maximal torus $T \subset G$ tame, $x$ in the apartment of $T$, and the Yu mock-exponential $e^T : \mathfrak{j}_x \to J_x$.

By [Adler §1.5(.2) + Cor 1.6.6] (the single-point iso + T-independence; the $\mathfrak j_x$-restricted version uses §1.9), $e_x$ induces an iso $\mathfrak{j}_x / \mathfrak{g}_{x, r+} \cong J_x / G_{x, r+}$, independent of $T$.

By the definition of generic quasi-character there is $X^* \in (\mathfrak{z}')^*$ of depth $-r$ with $$\hat \phi'_x(g) = \psi(\langle X^*, (e^T_x)^{-1}(g) \rangle) \qquad \forall g \in J_x.$$

Lemma (cf. Yu Lemma 9.3, Thm 9.4). For $x, y \in \mathcal{B}(G')$, $$I(\hat \phi_y|_{J_y}, \hat \phi_x|_{J_x}) = G_{x, s} G' G_{y, s}.$$
proof_html:
This proof reduces to two cited results: Adler §1.5(.2) (mock-exponential identity; the covariance statement at Lem 1.6.4 is a different ingredient) for the calculation step, and Yu Theorem 9.4 (as corrected / reformulated in [Dat–Fintzen 2026] Lem 2.6.6) for the geometric coset-meeting conclusion.

⚠️ Primary source: Dat–Fintzen 2026. Yu Thm 9.4 is one of the intertwiner statements whose original proof in Yu 2001 §9 was affected by the gap fixed in [Fintzen 2021]. The statement of Yu 9.4 is correct; the proof should reference DF / Fintzen 2021. See Fintzen 2021: correction to Yu's tame supercuspidal construction.

We give the reduction explicitly; for the cited results see Dat–Fintzen 2026: block decomposition + reduction to depth zero (tame) (primary) and Yu's tame supercuspidal construction (historical notation).

For $g \in I(\cdots)$, WLOG $gy$ and $x$ lie in the apartment of a common $T$, so $e^T : {}^g \mathfrak{j}_y \cap \mathfrak{j}_x \to {}^g J_y \cap J_x$ is a bijection. By the mock-exponential duality identity (cf. [Adler §1.5(.2)], not Adler Lem 1.6.4 — that lemma is a covariance identity, not the duality formula), for $Z \in {}^g \mathfrak{j}_y \cap \mathfrak{j}_x$, $$\hat \phi'_y({}^{g^{-1}} e^T(Z)) = \psi(\langle {}^g X^*, Z \rangle), \qquad \hat \phi'_x(e^T(Z)) = \psi(\langle X^*, Z \rangle).$$

Equating: $g \in I$ iff ${}^g X^ - X^ \in ({}^g \mathfrak{j}_y \cup \mathfrak{j}_x)^\perp = {}^g \mathfrak{j}^_y + \mathfrak{j}^_x$, i.e. ${}^g X^* + {}^g \mathfrak{j}_y^*$ meets $X^* + \mathfrak{j}_x^*$. The remainder follows the proof of Yu Thm 9.4 as corrected in [Fintzen 2021] / reformulated in [DF Lem 2.6.6]. $\square$

Alternative source: Dat–Fintzen

The two-term intertwiner identity is recast in [Dat–Fintzen 2026] as a geodesic-telescoping idempotent identity — DF Lemma 2.6.6 — and the specialization to two strata recovers Yu Thm 9.4. See the comparison table in [[node:references.yu_construction|yu_construction § Dat-Fintzen parallel]]. The DF derivation is purely Hecke-algebraic and avoids the explicit Yu mock-exponential bookkeeping; for verifying this lemma in detail, either source works.
